title: Medalist Anime Film's Teaser Reveals February 19 Opening
content:
Kadokawa revealed on Sunday a teaser trailer, teaser visual, character visuals, and the February 19 opening date for the upcoming anime film based on Tsurumaikada 's Olympic ice-skating manga Medalist .

Kodansha USA Publishing licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

Tsukasa, whose dreams were crushed. Inori, left to fend for herself. These two share a dream...and their tenacity may be the only thing that sees them through. Their destination? The ice...on the world's stage!

The film will tell a story set after the end of the television anime's second season.

The cast and staff from the TV anime return for the film.

The anime's first season premiered in Japan on the "NUMAnimation" programming block on TV Asahi and 23 affiliated channels in January 2025. Disney+ streamed the anime.

The second season debuted on January 24 on the "NUMAnimation" programming block on TV Asahi and 23 other affiliates channels, and ended on Sunday. Hulu is streaming the anime in the U.S., and Disney+ is streaming the anime in other countries and territories.

The second season featured the returning cast and staff. The first season's 3DCG environment supervisor Hazuki Nakamura was the art director for the new season, replacing Yōko Nakao . Kentaro Kashiwagi , the first season's 3DCG composite supervisor, was the second season's compositing director of photography, replacing Shin'ichi Komeya . Girl group HANA performed the opening theme song "Cold Night," and Conton Candy performed the ending theme song "Rookies."

Japanese figure skater Rika Hongo took part in the anime's motion capture filming alongside the first season's Akiko Suzuki .

Former Olympic skater Akiko Suzuki (returning for the second season) choreographed the skating routines in the first season of the anime, in collaboration with retired figure skater Yuhana Yokoi and active competitive figure skater Hinano Isobe.

Tsurumaikada launched the manga in Kodansha 's Afternoon magazine in May 2020. Kodansha published the 15th compiled book volume on July 22.

The manga won in the Best General Manga category of the 68th Shogakukan Manga Awards in 2023. The manga won Best General Manga at Kodansha 's 48th annual Manga Awards in May 2024.
author: ANN

title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend Film Unveils 2nd Trailer, Theme Song Artist
content:
The official website for Seishun Buta Yarō wa Dear Friend no Yume o Minai ( Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend ) film, the latest anime of Hajime Kamoshida 's Rascal Does Not Dream ( Seishun Buta Yarō or Aobuta) novel series, presented on Sunday the second full trailer, key visual, character visual for Miori Mitō, theme song, and information on an advance screening.

The trailer announces and previews the theme song "Suihei-sen wa Boku no Furukizu finale" (The Horizon Is My Old Wound: Finale) performed by the character Tōko Kirishima.

The staff will hold an advance screening of the film with the cast on October 4 at the Shinjuku Wald 9 theater in Tokyo.

The film will open in theaters in Japan on October 16. The new film is teased as taking the story towards its finale. (The film shares the same name as the 15th and final novel volume.)

The film's returning cast includes:

• Kaito Ishikawa as Sakuta Azusagawa

• Asami Seto as Mai Sakurajima

• Sora Amamiya as Uzuki Hirokawa

• Aya Yamane as Ikumi Akagi

• Konomi Kohara as Sara Himeji

• Manaka Iwami as Miori Mitō

• Reina Ueda as Nene Iwamizawa

• Nao Tōyama as Tomoe Koga

• Atsumi Tanezaki as Rio Futaba

• Maaya Uchida as Nodoka Toyohama

• Yurika Kubo as Kaede Azusagawa

• Inori Minase as Shōko Makinohara

Sōichi Masui returns to direct the film at CloverWorks . Masahiro Yokotani is also back to oversee and write the script, and Satomi Tamura is again designing the characters. The band fox capture plan also returns to compose the music. Aniplex is once again distributing the film.

Tōko Kirishima also performs the song "Turn the World Upside Down" in the film.

Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Bunny Girl-senpai no Yume wo Minai ), the first television anime based on the light novel series, premiered in Japan in October 2018 and aired for 13 episodes. The anime adapts the story up to the fifth novel volume. Aniplex of America streamed the series on Crunchyroll , Funimation , and other services.

Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Yume-Miru Shōjo no Yume wo Minai ), the anime film that adapts the the sixth and seventh light novel volumes in the franchise, opened in Japan in June 2019. Aniplex of America and Funimation Films screened the anime in the United States. Crunchyroll began streaming the film in June 2025 with both English subtitles and dub .

The first film Rascal Does Not Dream of a Sister Venturing Out opened in Japan in June 2023. The film sold 118,108 tickets in its first three days and earned 175,648,924 yen (about US$1.28 million) to rank #4 in its opening weekend. Rascal Does Not Dream of a Knapsack Kid , the second film, opened in Japan in December 2023, and ranked at #4 in its opening weekend. The film sold 119,000 tickets and earned 164,594,554 yen (about US$1.11 million) in its first three days.

Rascal Does Not Dream of Santa Claus ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Santa Claus no Yume wo Minai ), the television anime adapting the light novel series' "University Student Arc," premiered on July 5. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired, and is also streaming an English dub .

The original novel series has over 3 million copies in circulation. The Yen On imprint of Yen Press publishes the novel series, and Yen Press publishes Tsugumi Nanamiya 's manga adaptation. Yen On published the Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend novel volume on January 6.

title: Mushoku Tensei "Turning Point 4" Revealed as Title of Season 3 Episode 11
content:
Mushoku Tensei Season 3 has officially confirmed “Turning Point 4” as the title of its upcoming episode, Episode 11. As the name suggests, it means a turning point for Rudeus, and the previous episodes were all some of the most important ones in the anime. The new episode will premiere next Sunday on September 6.

Here’s a reminder of what happened in the previous “Turning Point” episodes.

“Turning Point 1” – Mushoku Tensei Season 1 Episode 11

In the first “Turning Point” episode, Mushoku Tensei Season 1 Episode 11, the teleportation incident happened. Prior to that, we saw Rudy celebrate his 10th birthday, make his promise with Eris, as well as numerous important character appearances. This was the episode where Kishirika Kishirisu, Orsted, Perugius Dola, and Almanfi appeared for the first time, although only Almanfi was named at the time.

At the end of the episode, we saw the incident that threw Rudy onto the Demon Continent, separating him from Sylphie and his family until much later in the anime. After the episode, Mushoku Tensei topped our weekly ranking in Winter 2021 Week 9 , ranking above Attack on Titan and JUJUTSU KAISEN .

“Turning Point 2” – Mushoku Tensei Season 1 Episode 21

Mushoku Tensei Season 1 Episode 21 was the second “Turning Point” episode, and it brought about Rudy’s encounter with Dragon God Orsted. This is widely considered as one of the best episodes of the anime so far due to the quality of the battle with Orsted. The character appears randomly and immediately causes tension with Eris and Ruijerd sensing the danger.

Rudy, as we later learn is due to a curse that doesn’t affect him, does not fear the Dragon God and carelessly ends up mentioning the name of Man-God. Man-God later explains that Orsted is cursed to be feared and hated by every person in the world, but it does not seem to affect otherworlders. He also says that he is the strongest and that he could even win against Laplace if he seriously tried.

This is also the episode where Nanahoshi was introduced. She is the one who ends up saving Rudy’s life, likely due to realizing that he also might be an otherworlder. After the episode, Mushoku Tensei topped our weekly ranking in Fall 2021 Week 10 , ranking above Demon Slayer and 86 EIGHTY-SIX .

“Turning Point 3” – Mushoku Tensei Season 2 Episode 18

The third and last “Turning Point” episode we’ve seen so far was Mushoku Tensei Season 3 Episode 18. Just like with the previous two, this episode also had major events for Rudy, although it was more of a setup for the upcoming reunion with Roxy and fight to save Paul which came later on. First, the episode starts with things going well. Nanahoshi is moving on with her research, Cliff is making progress with the item to help Elinalise, and Zanoba created his first figure and gifted it to Julie. Everything seems to be going up for Rudy, and this culminates in Sylphie telling him she’s pregnant with their first child. After an emotional moment between the two, they look forward to telling the others about it, commenting how Paul will be shocked to learn the news.

As Rudy comments that the paradise he dreamed of is right around the corner, the episode twists into what we’ve come to expect from its turning points with a letter from Geese.

“Zenith’s rescue difficult. Send help.”

This leads to Rudy setting out to help save Zenith, missing the birth of Lucy. It also lead to Paul’s eventual death and Rudy’s following trauma, as well as Roxy’s reappearance. Following the episode, Mushoku Tensei ranked third in Spring 2024 Week 6 .

Do you think “Turning Point 4” will be just as heavy as the previous ones? Let’s look forward to September 6 and the premiere of Mushoku Tensei Season 3 Episode 11.

Season 3 began with Volume 14, for which Seven Seas describes the story: Nanahoshi, Rudeus, and the rest of their group take a trip to Perugius’s mysterious floating fortress, seeking adventure and a once-in-a-lifetime chance to learn new magic. What they find instead is disaster as one of their number is struck down by a deadly illness. How far will Rudeus go to save a dear friend’s life?

You can also see the key visual for the third season.

The anime is based on a light novel by Rifujin na Magonote with Shirotaka’s illustrations. Seven Seas is publishing the light novel in English. The series is also launching a game titled Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation – Chronicle of Echoes this year. It is a free-to-play game with in-app purchases developed by ASOBIMO.

title: Jujutsu Kaisen Creator Returns With New Look at Yuta Ahead of Season 4
content:
Jujutsu Kaisen is now hard at work for its return with Season 4 of the anime, and the creator behind it all has returned with a cool new look at Yuta Okkotsu and Rika to help celebrate. Jujutsu Kaisen originally came to an end with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine back in 2024 . While the anime and official sequel series kept things going, Jujutsu Kaisen is planning to go even bigger to help celebrate its grand finale with a new exhibition opening later this year in Japan to show it all off.

“Jujutsu Kaisen Final Exhibition” is set to open in Shinjuku (where the final battle of the series takes place for the Shinjuku Showdown Arc) later this December, and it’s going to feature a closer look at all of creator Gege Akutami’s art from across the franchise’s history along with fun behind the scenes information for the creator’s process. To help kick off and tease this exhibition, Jujutsu Kaisen creator Gege Akutami has dropped a cool new look at Yuta and Rika that you can check out below.

When Does Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 Come Out?

But while both Jujutsu Kaisen and its official sequel, Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo , have officially finished Gege Akutami’s original story , the anime is gearing up for its own take on the series to bring the adaptation closer to its own grand finale too. Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 is currently in the works for a launch in the near future, but a concrete release window or date has been announced as of the time of this writing. There are still lots of questions surrounding this new season too as its development has been very mysterious.

Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 also revealed that Takeru Sato, who was an assistant director in Season 3, has been promoted to full series directing duties for the new episodes. Replacing Shota Goshazono seen in the third season, there are lots of hopes that this new season is going to be hitting it out of the park much like the first three seasons. And it’s a pretty high bar considering that the Culling Game Part 1 had some of the biggest episodes in the anime to date.

What’s Coming in Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4?

Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 will be picking up immediately after the events of the third season , and continue through the intense events of the Culling Game. After Yuji and Megumi had dealt with their first opponents in the deadly tournament, there are still a number of lingering characters who have yet to have their initial battles in the tournament thus far. We’re going to see all of them in action when the anime returns for the next phase of the Culling Game arc and kicks off what’s next.

This is the penultimate arc of Jujutsu Kaisen’ s original manga story, and the end of the arc directly leads into the final battle to come. There are some massive events already teased by the promotional materials revealed by the anime thus far, so you’re going to want to catch up with everything that’s happened in the anime now streaming with platforms like Crunchyroll, Netflix and more in the meantime.

title: Gintama Goes Full Demon Slayer With New Netflix Movie Release – Watch
content:
Gintama has returned to Netflix with a new feature film release you can stream now, and it’s going full Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba thanks to the popularity of the Infinity Castle trilogy. Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle has been one of the biggest anime films to hit theaters in recent memory , and did so well in Japan that it actually screened over there for nine long months. It’s not the only anime film to release in the past year, however, and Gintama hilariously had to call attention to it.

Gintama made its own return to theaters in the past year with a new feature film release remaking one of the standout arcs from the TV anime series, and it kicked things off in a hilarious way that only creator Hideaki Sorachi can. Opening with a scene that sees the main trio hoping to “trick” fans into thinking it’s actually the latest Demon Slayer movie, there are quite a few fun shout outs to the other franchise that gets you right in the mood for it all.

What to Know for Gintama’s New Movie on Netflix

Gintama the Movie 2026: Yoshiwara in Flames first hit theaters across Japan earlier this February , but now it’s available for streaming with Netflix with both Japanese and English language audio versions available. This shout out to Demon Slayer goes even further than expected as much of the cast from the Japanese language release actually make an appearance in both franchises too. The biggest of which is Gintoki voice actor Tomokazu Sugita, who also voices the Stone Hashira, Gyomei Himejima. It’s why Gintoki puts on his full outfit for the occasion.

Though this movie isn’t a Demon Slayer film, it’s got plenty for Gintama fans to enjoy. Gintama the Movie 2026: Yoshiwara in Flames is a remake of the TV anime arc of the same name , which took place between Episodes 139 through 146 of the series. Naoya Ando directed the new film for BN Pictures with Taku Kishimoto providing the script, and Shinji Takeuchi serving as chief animation director and providing character designs. There are even new scenes and enhanced sequences to make it a more complete experience for fans who had previously seen the TV series too.

What’s Next for Demon Slayer?

All this talk about Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle does make a lot of sense, however, as there are still lots of questions about what fans can hope to see from the next major film in the trilogy and where they can hope to see it . The second film has yet to confirm a release date or window as of the time of this writing, nor has it revealed any potential imagery for what’s to come. The first film had done so well in theaters across Japan that there was no real reason to rush ahead with the second.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle Part 2 will be picking up right from where the first film left off as Tanjiro Kamado and the others are in their final slate of fights against Muzan’s demonic forces. There have been some big deaths already through the first few fights, but there are even more losses on the way before it’s all over. Make sure to catch Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba ‘s TV anime releases now streaming with Netflix , but the first Infinity Castle film is only on Crunchyroll at the moment.

Though this movie isn’t a Demon Slayer film, it’s got plenty for Gintama fans to enjoy. Gintama the Movie 2026: Yoshiwara in Flames is a remake of the TV anime arc of the same name , which took place between Episodes 139 through 146 of the series. Naoya Ando directed the new film for BN Pictures with Taku Kishimoto providing the script, and Shinji Takeuchi serving as chief animation director and providing character designs. There are even new scenes and enhanced sequences to make it a more complete experience for fans who had previously seen the TV series too.
What’s Next for Demon Slayer?

All this talk about Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle does make a lot of sense, however, as there are still lots of questions about what fans can hope to see from the next major film in the trilogy and where they can hope to see it . The second film has yet to confirm a release date or window as of the time of this writing, nor has it revealed any potential imagery for what’s to come. The first film had done so well in theaters across Japan that there was no real reason to rush ahead with the second.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle Part 2 will be picking up right from where the first film left off as Tanjiro Kamado and the others are in their final slate of fights against Muzan’s demonic forces. There have been some big deaths already through the first few fights, but there are even more losses on the way before it’s all over. Make sure to catch Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba ‘s TV anime releases now streaming with Netflix , but the first Infinity Castle film is only on Crunchyroll at the moment.

title: Manga 'Kono Oto Tomare!' Ends in Three Chapters
content:
The official X account for manga creator Amyuu Sakura announced on Sunday that their Kono Oto Tomare! ( Stop This Sound! ) manga will end in three chapters.

The countdown includes the upcoming chapter in the October 2026 issue of Jump SQ. magazine, which is scheduled to release on September 4.

In the announcement, Amyu expressed deep gratitude to the readers, noting that Kono Oto Tomare! is their first serialized work. The author credited the fans' continuous support for allowing the series to run for so long and vowed to put their full effort into drawing the remaining chapters until the conclusion.

Amyuu began serializing the school music-themed manga in Jump SQ. magazine in August 2012. Shueisha published the 34th volume on June 4. Kono Oto Tomare! has a cumulative 7.5 million copies of its volumes in circulation.

The Kono Oto Tomare! - Tokise High School Koto Songs album released in March 2017 won an Excellence Prize at the 72nd National Arts Festival Record and the Traditional Japanese Music Album of the Year at the 32nd Gold Disc Awards .

Platinum Vision produced a 26-episode television anime adaptation that aired in two split-season courses between April and December 2019 . Crunchyroll streamed the anime with subtitles in multiple languages, as well as an English dub.

Synopsis Following the graduation of every other member of the Koto Music Club, Takezou Kurata is left alone as the new club president. Now burdened with the arduous task of rebuilding membership, he struggles to recruit anyone due to a lack of interest. Just as Kurata has lost nearly all hope in keeping the club alive, the feared delinquent Chika Kudou appears, claiming he will join and become the club president himself.

At first, Kurata refuses to admit such a troublesome person, aware of the dark rumors that have been circulating about Kudou. However, after discovering a more vulnerable side to Kudou and his mysterious connection to the club, Kurata rethinks his decision. The soon-to-be defunct club is saved with the help of koto prodigy Satowa Houzuki, who uses her charms to recruit Kudou's lively friends Saneyasu Adachi, Michitaka Sakai, and Kouta Mizuhara.

With sufficient numbers to retain the club's status, Houzuki declares that they will aim to become the best koto players in the nation, much to Kurata's dismay. This ragtag bunch of young musicians have a road filled with challenges and adversities ahead of them, and by overcoming their fears and differences, their aspirations may very well come true. [Written by MAL Rewrite]

title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend Reveals New Visual, Second Main Trailer and Theme Song
content:
Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend anime film revealed its second main trailer ahead of its October 16, 2026 theatrical premiere in Japan. The film will bring the Rascal Does Not Dream anime series to its conclusion.

The new trailer also features the movie’s theme song, “Turn the World Upside Down.” Ameko Kodama wrote the lyrics, while Hidehiro Kawai of fox capture plan composed and arranged the song.

A new key visual was also revealed.

The Rascal Does Not Dream light novel series was written by Hajime Kamoshida, while Keji Mizoguchi drew the illustrations for it. ASCII Media Works began publishing it under their Dengeki Bunko imprint in April 2014, releasing a total of 15 volumes. The final volume was released on October 10, 2024, marking the end of the novel after 10 years of serialization.

The entire anime adaptation so far has been animated by CloverWorks. It includes the Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai TV anime (covering volumes 1-5), as well as the previous three sequel movies. They are Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (volumes 6-7), Rascal Does Not Dream of a Sister Venturing Out (Volume 8), and Rascal Does Not Dream of a Knapsack Kid (Volume 9). The second TV anime season covered Volumes 10-13, while the Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend movie will adapt the rest.

title: Sagrada Reset Author Yutaka Kōno's Sayonara no Iikata Nante Shiranai Novel Series Gets Manga Adaptation
content:
Sagrada Reset novel author Yutaka Kōno announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Friday their Sayonara no Iikata Nante Shiranai (I Don't Know How to Say Goodbye) novel series will get a manga adaptation by Yukiko Seike ( 5 Centimeters per Second ) on Kodansha 's Comic Days platform in fall.

The novels are part of an overall "Kamisaki" series. Kōno first launched the franchise under the title Water & Biscuit no Theme with author Junichi Kawahashi (name romanization not confirmed) and Kadokawa published two volumes in 2017 and 2018 with illustrations by You Shiina . Kōno then relaunched the novel series as a solo author under the title Sayonara no Iikata Nante Shiranai in 2019. Shinchosha published the 11th volume on August 28 with illustrations by Hagu Koshijima .

The novels center on Ayumu Kaya, a second-year high school student. He receives a strange letter that states he has "earned the right to become a resident of Kamisaki." Ayumu has never heard of that town before, but he recognizes the mark on the letter's envelope — the same mark was left behind when his friend Toma disappeared two years earlier. Ayumu visits the designated apartment building to look for clues for what happened to his friend.

Ai Uzuki launched manga adaptation of Yutaka Kōno 's Inakunare, Gunjō ( Fragile Light of Pistol Star ) novel in Square Enix 's G Fantasy magazine in April 2018, and ended it in 2019. The novel debuted in 2014 as the first in Kōno's "Kaidantō" series of novels. The novel inspired a live-action film adaptation that opened in Japan in September 2019.

Kōno's Sagrada Reset novel series inspired a television anime in 2017, as well as two live-action films in the same year.

Seike's manga adaptation of Makoto Shinkai 's 5 Centimeters per Second film ran in Kodansha 's Afternoon magazine in 2010. Vertical and later Kodansha USA Publishing has released the manga in English digitally and in print.

title: 'Medalist Movie' Reveals New Staff, Trailer, February 19 Premiere
content:
The Medalist Special Exhibition 2026 event revealed the new staff, a second teaser visual (pictured), and special trailer for the anime sequel film adaptation of Tsurumaikada 's Medalist manga on Sunday. The anime movie is scheduled to premiere in Japanese theaters on February 19, 2027.

Staff Director: Yasutaka Yamamoto ( Noblesse ) Screenplay: Jukki Hanada ( Boku no Kokoro no Yabai Yatsu ) Character Design, Chief Animation Director: Chinatsu Kameyama ( Isekai wa Smartphone to Tomo ni. 2 ) Figure Skating Choreography: Suzuki Akiko ( Doraemon photography) Figure Skating Director, 3DCG Director: Koji 3DCG Visual Director: Takayuki Toda ( [Oshi no Ko] 2nd Season art design assistant) 3DCG Animation Supervisor: Shoutarou Hori ( Keikenzumi na Kimi to, Keiken Zero na Ore ga, Otsukiai suru Hanashi. ) 3DCG Producer: Kyouka Hagiwara NEW Color Design: Aiko Yamagami ( Dosanko Gal wa Namara Menkoi ) Art Director: Hazuki Nakamura Director of Photography: Ibuki Kunimasa NEW , Asuka Saitou NEW Editing: Tomoki Nagasaka ( Dance Dance Danseur ) Music: Yuuki Hayashi ( Haikyuu!! ) Sound Director: Yuuichi Imaizumi ( Kubo-san wa Mob wo Yurusanai ) Sound Effects: Kenji Koyama ( MF Ghost ) Animation Producer: Takasumi Miura Studio: ENGI Distribution: ANIMEC NEW

Note: The staff denoted with the legend NEW are new in their respective roles .

Produced by animation studio ENGI, the first season aired in Winter 2025, followed by a second season in Winter 2026. Disney+ streamed the anime worldwide, with Hulu handling its U.S. release alongside an English dub.

Tsurumaikada began drawing the drama sports manga in Afternoon magazine in May 2020. Kodansha published the 15th volume on July 22.

Kodansha USA licensed the manga in English in March 2021 and digitally released the 14th volume on May 12.

title: Medalist Movie Reveals New Teaser Trailer, Visual, February 19, 2027 Premiere
content:
Medalist sequel anime movie revealed a new trailer and visual, along with a February 19, 2027 premiere date. The movie was announced earlier this year, while the news came immediately after the TV anime’s second season concluded on March 22.

The anime adaptation by studio ENGI premiered in January 2025, running for a total of 12 episodes. Season 2 was announced immediately after the finale, running for 9 episodes. The anime is streaming on Disney+ (Disney Plus).

You can watch the new trailer for the upcoming movie below.

Yasutaka Yamamoto directed the Medalist anime, with Chinatsu Kameyama as the character designer and Jukki Hanada in charge of the series composition and screenplay. You can see the movie’s new visual below.

ALSO READ: Yuzuru Hanyu Mesmerizes on Ice as Kenshi Yonezu Sings Medalist OP “BOW AND ARROW” in New MV

Medalist is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Tsurumaikada. It has been serialized in Kodansha’s Monthly Afternoon since May 2020, and it has 15 compiled volumes as of July 2026. The manga series also won at the 68th Shogakukan Manga Award for the general category. Kodansha licensed it in English, and they’ve been releasing it since May 2021 . The story follows Tsukasa, a man whose dreams of competitive skating were shattered, and Inori, a girl determined to make it to the world stage despite starting out late. United by the shared goal, they embark on the difficult journey of figure skating.
